title: Jump-Start a Car
summary: Dead battery, good donor car. Connect positive to positive, negative to ground — in the right order.

learn.heading: What you're looking at
learn.body: You need jumper cables and a donor vehicle with a good battery. Both cars off when you connect. Red cable = positive (+). Black cable = negative (−). The dead car's battery may have corrosion on the terminals — clean enough to get a solid clamp bite.

learn.heading: What can hurt you
learn.body: Batteries vent hydrogen — sparks can ignite it. Connect in the right order to avoid sparks near the battery. Never let red and black clamps touch each other while connected to a battery. The final negative clamp goes on an unpainted metal ground on the dead car's engine block — not on the dead battery's negative post if you can avoid it.
learn.callout: If either battery is cracked, leaking, or frozen, stop. Jumping it is dangerous.

learn.heading: The steps
learn.body:
1. Park donor car nose-to-nose or side-by-side, close enough for cables. Both engines off.
2. Red clamp to dead battery positive (+).
3. Other red clamp to donor battery positive (+).
4. Black clamp to donor battery negative (−).
5. Other black clamp to unpainted metal on dead car's engine block (ground point).
6. Start donor car, let it run a minute.
7. Start dead car. If it doesn't crank, wait another minute — don't grind the starter.
8. Once running, remove cables in reverse order: black ground on dead car, black on donor, red on donor, red on dead.
9. Keep the jumped car running 20+ minutes to recharge, or drive it.

practice.prompt: Put the jumper cable connection steps in order.

steps.text: Red clamp to dead battery positive (+)
Red clamp to donor battery positive (+)
Black clamp to donor battery negative (−)
Black clamp to engine block ground on dead car

practice.failMessage: Red dead, red donor, black donor, black ground on the dead car. That order keeps sparks away from the dead battery.

practice.prompt: Tap where the last (fourth) black clamp should go.

parts.label: Unpainted engine block bolt on dead car

practice.failMessage: Last clamp goes to a ground point on the dead car's engine block — not the radiator or donor positive.

practice.prompt: What's wrong with this jump-start setup?

options.text: Red and black cable clamps touching each other while connected
Both engines off during cable hookup
options.feedback: Engines off during hookup is correct.

options.text: Donor car running before starting the dead car
options.feedback: Letting the donor run before cranking the dead car is the right move.

practice.failMessage: Touching clamps = dead short. Sparks, melted cables, possible battery explosion.
